turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I'm here because I went for a physical to get cleared for a new logistics job, moving freight. The clinic there said my weight was too low and wouldn't sign off on me. I don't really get it, to be honest. To me, I just look lean. I need to be light and quick on my feet to do the work, you know? But they told me I had to come see a doctor about it.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient reports being referred for evaluation because an occupational health clinic found their weight was too low to clear them for work.

turns.doctor_question: Have you lost weight recently without trying to, or has your weight stayed about the same over the last few months?
turns.patient_response: I haven't really been losing weight without trying, no. I mean, I guess I've dropped a few pounds over the last several months, but my weight has mostly stayed around the same. I just try to keep myself in shape for the work.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me about your appetite and whether you've had any changes in your eating habits recently?
turns.patient_response:
My appetite is... well, it's fine, I guess. I just don't need a whole lot. My habits haven't really changed recently, I just keep things pretty simple so I don't get weighed down. 

Most days I just keep it to black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna. That gets me through. And if I’m not moving freight on a shift—like if I'm off that day—I just tell myself I don’t need a real meal anyway, since I'm not doing the heavy lifting.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient reports severely restricting daily food intake to black coffee and minimal items like a single boiled egg or tuna, actively avoiding full meals.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me more about the weight loss you mentioned — when did it start, and how much weight do you think you've lost?
turns.patient_response:
I don't really have an exact number for you, to be honest. I don't step on a scale at home or keep track of it like that. 

I guess it just started gradually over... well, maybe the last year or so? I just noticed my work pants getting a bit looser, so I had to pull my belt tighter. But I couldn't tell you exactly how many pounds I've dropped. Like I said, I just focus on staying lean so I can keep up with the work.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me about your typical weight over the years — have you always been this lean, or is this a recent change in your body type?
turns.patient_response: I've never really been a big guy, if that's what you mean. I've always been pretty average, I guess. But... well, I suppose I used to have a bit more meat on my bones a few years back. It's just over the last year or two that I've gotten this lean. It wasn't like I woke up one day and looked different, it just sort of happened over time with how I've been eating and working. So yeah, I've always been on the smaller side, but being this thin is definitely more recent.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever intentionally limit your food intake because you're worried about gaining weight or because you think you need to stay as lean as possible for your job?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do limit what I eat, mostly because... well, I just get worried about putting weight on. Like, if I eat something heavy—rice, bread, or anything greasy—I just can't stop thinking about it. I feel like it's going to just sit on me right away. 

So if I do eat something like that, I usually end up checking the scale or tightening my belt the next morning, just to make sure I didn't let myself go. I just need to keep it under control.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly confirms getting worried about putting weight on, obsessively thinking about heavy foods immediately causing weight gain, and checking the scale or belt to ensure they have not gained weight.

turns.doctor_question: When you talk about worrying about gaining weight, is it more about how you see yourself, or is it mainly because of what you think the job requires of you?
turns.patient_response:
It's... well, it's mostly about how I see myself, I guess. I mean, the job is part of it, but when I look in the mirror... especially at my stomach and my waist... I just feel like I need to be smaller. Tight-looking, you know? 

If I'm not, I just feel like I'm not that same disciplined man I used to be out on the warehouse floor. It's like my body is telling me I'm getting soft or letting myself go, and I just can't stand that. So I have to keep it in check.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient describes judging his personal discipline and self-worth based on whether his stomach and waist look small and tight in the mirror, confirming undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt that your weight or body shape has a strong influence on how you feel about yourself, to the point where it affects your daily life or how you see who you are?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it definitely does. Like I was saying, when I look in the mirror, it's my stomach and my waist that really get to me. If I don't look small and tight... I don't know, I just feel like I'm losing who I am. I spent years on the warehouse floor being the strong, disciplined guy who could handle anything. If my body doesn't look the part, if I look soft, I feel like I'm failing. It just completely ruins how I see myself, so I have to make sure I stay lean.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient confirms that his body shape and weight have an undue influence on his self-worth and identity, stating that not looking small and tight ruins how he sees himself and makes him feel like a failure.

turns.doctor_question: Would you say that your weight or body shape has a major impact on how you feel about yourself overall?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, like I was just saying, it really does. It dictates pretty much everything about how I feel. When I look in the mirror, especially right at my stomach and waist, if I'm not smaller and tight-looking... I just feel like I'm not that same disciplined man I used to be out on the warehouse floor. So, yes, my shape absolutely determines how I value myself overall.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient explicitly confirms that his body shape and stomach/waist appearance dictate how he values himself and feels overall.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever do anything like exercising a lot, making yourself sick, or taking medications to control your weight or body shape?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't do any of that. I mean, my work keeps me moving around a lot, hauling freight and all, but I'm not doing extra workouts or going to a gym. And I definitely don't make myself sick or take any kind of pills for it. I just don't do those things.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient denies engaging in excessive exercise or extra workouts to control weight.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies self-induced vomiting or taking pills or medications to control weight.
